25th January 1917.

Sir,
The removal of Sung Hung Yi 孫洪伊 from the post of Minister of Home Affairs caused a great deal of alarm in Koh Ming Tong circles. That believes that its opponents are trying to reduce it to impotence and endeavours are to be made to regain the power which has been lost by the dismissal of Sung Hung Yi and in other ways.
Sung Hung Yi, Li Lih Chun 李烈鈞, Tang Shao Yi 唐紹儀, Sun Yat Sen 孫逸仙 and Tang Jen Fung 譚人鳳 all of whom are in this locality are reported to be plotting another rebellion which will comprise the provinces of Kwangtung, Kiangsi, Hunan and Chekiang and which is timed to start in the month of April or May 1917.
A declaration is being prepared which will be promulgated [涂改] and in which the Premier Tuan Chi Jui 段祺瑞 will be accused of having instigated the formation of the Provincial League at Hsuchow 徐州 with its unavowed object of bringing about the dissolution of the present Parliament. He will also be accused of having a representative at the secret conferences of the above mentioned League in the form of Zee Su Tsung 徐樹錚, the ex-Secretary of the Cabinet and of having shaped the proceedings to suit his own ends as well as the aims of his party.

Your obedient servant,

[签名]

Chief Detective Inspector.

Captain Superintendent of Police.

先生，
孙洪伊被免去内务总长一职，在国民党圈内引起了极大恐慌。该党认为其对手正试图使其陷入瘫痪，并正努力通过其他方式夺回因孙洪伊被免职而失去的权力。
据悉，目前均在本地的孙洪伊、李烈钧、唐绍仪、孙中山和谭人凤正在策划另一次叛乱，范围将涵盖广东、江西、湖南和浙江四省，预定于1917年4月或5月发动。
一份宣言正在起草中，即将颁布[涂改]，其中将指控总理段祺瑞煽动在徐州成立省区联合会，其未公开的目的是导致现任国会解散。还将指控他以内阁前秘书徐树铮为代表，参加上述联合会的秘密会议，并操纵议事进程以迎合其个人目的及其党派目标。

January 25th 1917

Sir,
Certain members of the Koh Ming Tong in this
locality are endeavouring to frame an impeachment
which will be sent to the Central Government against
the Tuchun of Chekiang province, Yang Sin Teh.
He is accused amongst other things of having issued
a huchao to a subject of one of the belligerent
nations in order that he might buy arms and
ammunition in Shanghai and transport them to
his own country.
The Koh Ming Tong are being instigated to act
by Germans who are supplying the information on
which the proceedings are being taken.

Your Obedient Servant,

Chief Detective Inspector.

Captain Superintendent of Police.

January 25th 7.

Sir,
In continuation of a previous report which
was to the effect that Dr. Sun Yat Sen was
endeavouring to induce a number of Chinese
emigrants in the Strait Settlements to forward a telegram
to the Peking Government asking for the return
of money borrowed from them by the doctor
in connection with the late rebellion, I beg to
state that information has now been received that
a joint telegram signed by several emigrants who
were on friendly terms with Dr. Sun Yat Sen
has been despatched to Peking asking why certain
M.P.s objected repaying the money and why they
never interfered with the misappropriation
of money by the late Yuan Shih Kai in connection
with the monarchical movement.
The telegram points out that the request of
the various leaders in the present instance
was quite reasonable as the money was spent
in the public service.
It is reported that Sun Wen 孙文 and Nyi
Teh Sun, 钮永建 have demanded $2,700,000
Tan Yin Poong 谭人凤
former defence Commiss-
ioner of Yangtse 300,000
Li Lieh Chun 李烈钧
former Tutuh of Kiangsi 500,000
Wu Ta Chow 吴大洲
Commander of the
Rebel army in Shantung 1,400,000

They hope to get the money and if they do
will devote it to raising another rebellion.
President Li Yuen Hung has consented to
pay the money demanded by Dr. Sun Wen if he
can produce evidence of its expenditure and
the Governor of Shantung is instructed to consider
the request of Wu Ta Chow and to note that
money if it can be raised in that province is only to be
used to bring about the disbandment of rebel soldiers there.
Your Obedient Servant,
Captain Superintendent of Police. MA
C.P.I.

My dear Sir Everard,              Confidential.
            With reference to the report that
Tang Shao Yi, Sun Yat Sen, Sung Hung Ti and other
revolutionary leaders are combining together in
some way to cause trouble locally and in the
Chekiang province, I have gone carefully into the
matter and cannot find any confirmation of this
report.
    On December .. it was reported to me that Sun
Yat Sen, Tang Shao Yi and other revolutionary
leaders were interesting themselves in the Chekiang
affair and were going to do their utmost to keep the
Military power in the hands of their party.
    It appears that General Yang Sin Teh, the new
Tuchun, has succeeded in installing one half of a
Mixed Brigade of Northern troops inside the City
of Hangchow while the other half will remain
outside the town for the time being. General ..
continue in the City of Hangchow and the chances
of a rising on the part of the Chekiang soldiery
are not to be considered to be very remote.
    The most of the opposition to a garrison of
Northern men under a Northern leader comes from the
officers of the local troops and from the civil
and Police officials who fear that they will

            鉴于有关唐绍仪、孙中山、孙洪蒂及其他
革命领袖正以某种方式联合起来，在本地及
浙江省制造麻烦的报告，我已仔细调查此事，
但未能找到任何证实该报告的依据。
    12月..日，有人向我报告称，孙中山、唐绍仪
及其他革命领袖正关注浙江事务，并将竭尽全力
将军事权力保留在其党派手中。
    看来，新任督军杨善德将军已成功将一半北洋
混成旅部署在杭州城内，而另一半暂时留在城外。
..将军继续留在杭州城内，浙江军队发生兵变的可能
性被认为并非遥不可及。
    对由北方领袖率领的北方驻军的大部分反对意见来自
当地部队军官以及文职和警务官员，他们担心自己将

2

lost their posts and are consequently secretly
inciting and stirring up strife and hostility while
ostensibly professing to be friendly to the Government.
The openly hostile persons are the extreme members
of the Koh Ming Tang who have no positions at all,
the present members of the Provincial Assembly, and
members of certain educational associations.
The Koh Ming Tang adherents under Sun Yat Sen, Tang
Shao Yi, Tsung Bing Ling and others believe that if
they can start an agitation sufficiently strong,
the Tuchun nominated by the Government will leave the
province after the example of Tang Hsiang Ling, Tuchun
of Hunan who, last year, was scared by the exhibition
of force which they displayed and fled from Changsha.
The only way in which the Koh Ming Tang Chieftains
in Shanghai are believed to be aiding their party
in Hangchow at the present moment is by sending paid
and professional agitators who are expected to work
amongst the soldiery with the object of inciting them
to rise in sufficient strength to daunt the government
and deter it from carrying out its present policy.
The Tuchuns of the provinces of Hokhien, Kiangsi
and Anhui are all being warned to be in readiness to
aid in suppressing any rebellion which might materialise,
and their forces together with those of the new Tuchun
and those of the garrison of Shanghai are considered
to be quite strong enough to cope with any emergency
which may arise. The arrangements for a military
concentration in Chekiang from all sides in case of a
rising, have the approval of the Vice President, Feng
Kuo Chang, who will reinforce the troops here if their

2

失去职位，因此表面上宣称对政府友好，暗地里却
煽动和挑起争端与敌意。
公开持敌对态度的人是国民党的极端分子，他们没有任何
职位，还有省议会现任议员以及某些教育团体的成员。
孙中山、唐绍仪、宗秉灵（音译）等人麾下的国民党
追随者认为，如果他们能发起足够强大的 agitation（煽动/运动），
政府任命的督军将会像去年湖南督军汤芗铭那样离开该省，
汤芗铭当时被他们展示的武力所吓倒，逃离了长沙。
目前认为上海的国民党首领援助其在杭州的党派的
唯一方式，是派遣受雇的职业煽动者，预计这些人将在
士兵中开展工作，目的是煽动他们发动足够强大的兵变，
以震慑政府并阻止其执行现行政策。
福建、江西和安徽各省的督军均已接到警告，要随时准备
协助镇压任何可能发生的叛乱，他们的部队连同新督军的
部队以及上海驻军的力量，被认为完全足以应对任何可能
出现的紧急情况。副总统一职的冯国璋批准了在发生兵变
时从各方在浙江进行军事集结的安排，如果这里的部队
因随后派遣分队去援助他们在杭州的同志而

numbers are depleted by the subsequent despatch of de-
tachments to the aid of their comrades in Hangchow.
On January 12 General Yang Sin Teh left for Hangchow
accompanied by his bodyguard. A telegram was received
in the evening to the effect that he had arrived
safely at his destination and had installed himself
at Hangchow as Tuchun of Chekiang province.
The Police can obtain no information of the report
that Sun Yat Sen, Tang Shao Yi and Sung Hung Yi are
conspiring with certain foreigners to start trouble in
the province of Chekiang. The only Europeans with
whom these so-called Tang leaders associate are the
French, and the latter are not likely to be in favour
of stirring up any rebellion in this vicinity at the
present moment.
Sung Hung Yi is reported to be in Hankow.
On January 13 further reports were received that
on account of financial difficulties Sun Yat Sen and
his followers have apparently given up the attempt to
engineer a rising in Chekiang.
A number of men who claim Tsang Sing Ling as their
Chief and who are mostly natives of Chekiang appear to
be working independently, and they are trying to
persuade the Chamber of Commerce, Hangchow, to start
a movement to cause the people to refrain from paying
taxes.
Chen Ching Tao, the Financial Minister, is promising
financial aid to Sun Yat Sen. The latter is attempting
to induce certain Chinese in the Straits Settlements
to request the Peking Government to refund them money
borrowed by him in connexion with the last revolution.
According to information received from certain
railway employees, who profess to be acquainted with

人数减少，他将增援这里的部队。
1月12日，杨善德将军在卫队陪同下前往杭州。当晚收到
一封电报，称他已安全抵达目的地，并在杭州就任浙江
省督军。
警方无法获取有关孙中山、唐绍仪和孙洪伊正与某些外国人
勾结在浙江省制造麻烦的报告的情报。这些所谓的唐派领袖
交往的唯一欧洲人是法国人，而法国人目前不太可能支持在
这一地区煽动任何叛乱。
据报道，孙洪伊在汉口。
1月13日收到进一步报告，称由于财政困难，孙中山及其
追随者显然已放弃在浙江策划兵变的企图。
一批自称以臧星灵（音译）为首领的人，大多为浙江籍，
似乎正在独立行动，他们正试图说服杭州商会发起一场运动，
促使民众拒绝纳税。
财政总长陈锦涛正承诺向孙中山提供财政援助。后者正试图
诱使海峡殖民地的某些中国人请求北京政府退还他在上次革命
期间向他们借用的款项。
根据自称熟悉情况的某些铁路员工提供的信息，

the political situation, the representati of from Tuchuns
of the Northern provinces - who attended the celebration
of Vice President Feng Kuo Chang at Nanking - went on
January 6 to Hauchow at the request of Generals Chang
Hsun and Chi Chi Chung. It is alleged that Chang
Hsun has been endeavouring, with the help of Liang
Chi Chao who is now in Peking, to cause the removal
of three Ministers viz. Chen Ching Tao, the Minister of
Finance, Chang Tau Tsun, the Minister of Justice and
Yan Lien Yuen, the Minister of Education. They are
members of the Hoh Ling Tang party and he proposes to
replace them with the followers of Liang Chi Chao or with
the supporters of the Premier.

No one has visited Sun Yat Sen.

A watch has been kept on the house of Tang Shao Yi
since January 10 and the principal visitor appears to
be the German Dr. Krieg who is apparently visiting
some person who is ill in the house. Three Japanese,
who appeared to be curio dealers, also called several
times, and a number of well dressed foreigners who
came in the car licensed in the name of the Russian
Consul-General. Attached I forward you copies of
detective reports giving details of the watch.

The latest report received this morning regarding
Sung Hung Yi is that he has secretly arrived in
Shanghai from Hankow and Nanking, and is staying at
No. 4 Route Vallon in the French Concession. Further
enquiries will be made regarding this.

政治局势方面，来自北方各省督军的代表——他们曾出席在南京举行的副总统冯国璋的庆典——应张勋和倪嗣冲将军的要求，于1月6日前往徐州。据称，张勋一直在目前身处北京的梁启超的帮助下，试图罢免三位部长，即财政总长陈锦涛、司法总长章宗祥和教育总长范源濂。他们是研究系（Hoh Ling Tang party）成员，他提议用梁启超的追随者或总理的支持者来取代他们。

Report on Watch on Tang Shao Yi.

The watch on the house of Tang Shao Yi has been continued

inside. A little later a Chinese delivered two parcels at

Sir,
    Regarding attached, as far as can be learned Sun Hung
Yi 孙洪伊 a native of Chihli, who was minister of
Home Affairs from the time Li Yuen Hung became President
until about 3 months ago, is not in Shanghai. Sun has
been for many years connected with the Kuomintang party
and is an active opponent of the Peking clique. It is
expected that he will come to Shanghai soon.
    According to a telegram of the Eastern News Agency
appearing in the Shanghai Times on 12th inst, Sun arrived
in Hankow from Peking on 11th instant.
    Tang Shao Yi visited No.198 Range Road, his concubine's

leave his house since the watch started. The only foreigners
seen to visit his place were three Japanese who entered

POLICE FORCE,

January 13th 1918.

Sir,
On account of financial difficulties Dr. Sun
Yat Sen and his followers have apparently given
up the attempt to engineer a rising in Chekiang.
A number of men who claim Tsang Bing Ling 章炳麟
as their Chief and who are mostly natives of
Chekiang appear to be working independently
and they are trying to persuade the Chamber
of Commerce Hangchow to start a movement to cause
the people to refrain from paying taxes.
Chen Ching Tao 陈锦涛 the Financial Minister
is promising financial aid to Dr. Sun Yat Sen.
The latter is attempting to induce certain Chinese
in the Settlements to request the Peking
Government to refund them money borrowed by
him in connection with the last revolution.
According to information received from
certain railway employees who profess to be
acquainted with the political situation the
representatives from Tuchuns of the Northern
provinces who attended the celebration of Vice
President Feng Kuo Chang at Nanking, went on the
6th inst to Hsuchow 徐州 at the request of Generals
Chang Hsun and Nyi Chi Chung. It is alleged that
Chang Hsun has been endeavouring with the help
of Liang Chi Chao 梁启超 who is now at Peking
to cause the removal of three Ministers viz
Chen Ching Tao 陈锦涛 the Minister of Finance,
Chang Yau Tsun 章宗祥 the Minister of Justice
and Van Lie n Yuen 范廉元 the Minister of Education.
They are members of the Kuomintang party
and he proposes to replace them with the
followers of Liang Chi Chao or with the
supporters of the Premier.

Your Obedient Servant,

Chief Detective Inspector.

Captain Superintendent of Police.

1918年1月13日。

先生，
由于财政困难，孙中山博士及其追随者似乎已放弃在浙江发动起义的企图。一批自称以章炳麟（Tsang Bing Ling 章炳麟）为首领、且多为浙江籍的人士似乎在独立行动，他们正试图说服杭州商会发起一场运动，促使民众拒绝纳税。
财政总长陈锦涛（Chen Ching Tao 陈锦涛）承诺向孙中山博士提供财政援助。后者正试图诱使租界内的某些中国人请求北京政府偿还他在上次革命期间以个人名义借入的款项。

Shanghai Municipal Council.

January 11th 1917

Sir,
In continuation of my report of December 29th
last wherein it was stated that Sun Yat Sen,
Tang Shao Yi and other Koh Ming Tong leaders
were interesting themselves in the Chekiang
affair and were going to do their utmost to
keep the Military power in the hands of their
party, I beg to add, that General Yang Sin
Toh 楊善德 the new Tuchun has succeeded in
installing one half of a Mixed Brigade of
Northern troops inside the City of Hangchow
while the other half will remain outside the
town for the time being. General Yang will
depart for his new post in a day or two accompanied
by a bodyguard of selected soldiers.
Discussions continue in the City of
Hangchow and the chances of a rising on the part
of the Chekiang soldiery are not considered to
be very remote.
The most of the opposition to a garrison
of Northern men under a Northern leader comes
from the officers of the local troops and from
the Civil and Police officials who fear that they
will lose their posts and are consequently
secretly inciting and stirring up strife and
hostility while ostensibly professing to
be friendly to the Government.
The openly hostile persons are the extreme
members of the Koh Ming Tong who have no positions
at all, the present members of the Provincial
Assembly, and members of certain educational
associations.
The Koh Ming Tong adherents under Sun Yat
Sen, Tang Shao Yi, Tsang Bing Ling and others
believe that if they can start an agitation
sufficiently strong that the Tuchun nominated
by the Government will leave the province after

先生：
继我去年12月29日的报告（其中指出孙中山、唐绍仪及其他国民党领导人正关注浙江事务，并将竭尽全力使军事权力掌握在其党派手中）之后，谨此补充，新任督军杨善德已成功将一个混成旅的一半北洋部队部署在杭州城内，而另一半暂时留在城外。杨将军将在一两天内由精选士兵组成的卫队陪同，前往新职。
杭州市内的讨论仍在继续，浙江军队发生起义的可能性被认为并非遥不可及。
对由北方领袖率领的北方驻军的大部分反对意见，来自当地军队的军官以及文职和警务官员，他们担心会失去职位，因此表面上宣称对政府友好，暗地里却在煽动和挑起纷争与敌意。
公开持敌对态度的人是那些毫无职位的国民党极端分子、省议会现任议员以及某些教育团体的成员。
孙中山、唐绍仪、臧炳灵 (Tsang Bing Ling) 等人麾下的国民党追随者相信，如果他们能发起足够强大的 agitation（煽动/骚乱），政府任命的督军就会像湖南督军汤芗铭那样离开该省；汤芗铭去年因他们展示的武力威慑而感到惊恐，逃离了长沙。
